walkthroughs.body_html:
Before 1832 only about 3% of adults could vote. Rotten boroughs like Old Sarum returned MPs with 7 voters.

After Peterloo (1819) and unrest, the 1832 Great Reform Act abolished rotten boroughs and added middle-class men. The electorate grew from 400,000 to 650,000.

The People's Charter (1838) demanded universal male suffrage and the secret ballot.

Three petitions (1839, 1842, 1848) were rejected. But by 1918 five of the six demands were law. The 1867 Reform Act doubled the electorate; the 1884 Act tripled it again.

Emmeline Pankhurst founded the WSPU in 1903 — 'Deeds not words'.

Emily Davison died at the 1913 Derby. The 1918 Representation of the People Act gave women over 30 with property the vote. The 1928 Equal Franchise Act gave all women the vote at 21 — equal to men.

mcqs.q: When did women get the vote on equal terms with men?
What did the 1832 Great Reform Act actually do?
options: It abolished rotten boroughs, redistributed seats to industrial towns, and extended the vote to about 1 in 5 adult men — still far short of democracy.
The 1832 Reform Act allowed women to vote for the first time.
The 1832 Reform Act gave the vote to all working men.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.

mcqs.q: What did the 1928 Equal Franchise Act do?
options: The 1918 Representation of the People Act gave all women the vote.
It gave women the vote on the same terms as men — all adults over 21 — completing the process begun in 1918, which had only enfranchised women over 30 with property.
The 1832 Reform Act allowed women to vote for the first time.
The 1928 Act gave women in Britain the vote for the first time.

mcqs.q: What did Magna Carta actually do in 1215?
options: It was a peace treaty between King John and rebel barons protecting baronial privileges and limiting arbitrary royal taxation and imprisonment — it was annulled within months.
The 1928 Act gave women in Britain the vote for the first time.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
Magna Carta gave ordinary English people democratic rights and freedom.
